qs.q: An ATPL applicant (India) shall have completed in aeroplanes not less than:
o: 100 h of instrument time, of which not more than 50 h may be instrument ground time
150 h of instrument time, of which not more than 75 h may be ground time
100 h of instrument time, of which not more than 30 h may be ground time
qs.ex: Indian rules: 100 h instrument, at least 50 h in actual flight.

qs.q: A licence holder must tell the authority of an illness that makes them unable to exercise the licence for a period of at least how many days?
The Chicago Convention Annex on Personnel Licensing is:
o: Annex 1
Annex 2
Annex 11

qs.q: The minimum age for a PPL is:
o: 18 years
17 years
21 years

qs.q: The privileges of a CPL(A) holder include:
o: PIC of any aeroplane in commercial air transport
PIC of any single-pilot aeroplane, other than in commercial air transport
PIC of any aeroplane up to 5,700 kg all-up weight that is entered in the aircraft rating of the licence

qs.q: The period of currency of a medical assessment begins:
o: When the licence is issued or renewed
From the date of the medical examination
When the licence is delivered to the pilot

qs.q: Type ratings shall be established:
o: For any type whenever the authority considers it necessary
All of these
For aircraft certificated for a minimum crew of at least two pilots

qs.q: A CPL holder acting as co-pilot performing PIC duties under the supervision of a check pilot is credited:
o: In full, but not more than 300 h, towards a higher licence
With 50% towards a higher licence
In full towards the total time required for a higher licence

qs.q: For an instrument rating, a PPL or CPL holder must have completed how many hours of cross-country flight time as PIC?
An ATPL applicant (India) shall have completed in aeroplanes not less than:
o: 75 h of night flight as PIC or co-pilot
100 h of night flight as PIC or co-pilot
100 h of night flight only as PIC

qs.q: To exercise CPL(A) privileges at night, the applicant must have completed in aeroplanes not less than:
o: 5 h of night flight including 3 take-offs and 3 landings as PIC
5 h of night flight including 5 take-offs and 5 landings as PIC
5 h of night flight including 10 take-offs and 10 landings as PIC

qs.q: A CPL(A) applicant shall have completed in aeroplanes not less than:
o: 150 h of flight time and 100 h as PIC
200 h of flight time and 70 h as PIC
200 h of flight time and 100 h as PIC

qs.q: A CPL applicant (India) shall have completed in aeroplanes not less than:
o: 20 h of instrument instruction, of which not more than 10 h ground time
20 h of instrument instruction, of which not more than 5 h ground time
10 h of instrument time, of which not more than 5 h on an approved simulator

qs.q: Under Annex 1, an instrument rating applicant must show the ability to fly the aircraft by instruments alone with an engine:
o: Multi-engine / inoperative or simulated inoperative
Land / inactive
Amphibious / inactive or simulated inactive

qs.q: A CPL(A) applicant must have at least ___ h of cross-country flight as PIC, including a cross-country flight of at least ___, with full-stop landings at two different aerodromes.
o: 15 h and 540 km (300 NM)
20 h and 540 km (300 NM)
10 h and 270 km (150 NM)

qs.q: A CPL applicant must hold a current:
o: Class 1 medical assessment
Class 3 medical assessment
Medical class prescribed by the issuing State

qs.q: The minimum age for a CPL applicant is:
For public transport flights (with an ATPL), the minimum and maximum ages are:
o: 21 and 65
16 and 60
18 and 60

qs.q: Which Annex contains the minimum specifications for a crew licence to be valid internationally?
o: Annex 1
Annex 3
Annex 4

qs.q: Applicants for which licences must speak and understand radiotelephony English to the level set by DGCA?
o: PPL, CPL, ATPL, flight navigator and flight engineer
PPL, CPL and ATPL only
PPL only

qs.q: The privileges of a PPL holder are to act as:
o: PIC or co-pilot of any aeroplane, with no passengers
PIC or co-pilot of any aeroplane, carrying passengers without remuneration
PIC or co-pilot of any aeroplane on aerial work for remuneration

qs.q: A CPL holder over 40 flying a single-pilot helicopter on charter has a medical validity of:
o: 6 months
12 months
12 months if not carrying VIPs
